from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import re
from .fenced_code import parse_fenced_code
from .html_blocks import parse_html_block

from .references import extract_definitions
from .setext import parse_setext
from .indented_code import _strip_columns


@dataclass
class Block:
    """A minimal block node retaining source for later inline parsing."""

    kind: str
    children: list["Block"] = field(default_factory=list)
    literal: str = ""
    level: int | None = None
    info: str = ""
    ordered: bool = False
    start: int = 1
    tight: bool = True

    @property
    def type(self) -> str:
        """Compatibility name for the block node's kind."""
        return self.kind


@dataclass
class Document:
    """Ordered block tree and document-wide reference definitions."""

    children: list[Block] = field(default_factory=list)
    references: dict[str, object] = field(default_factory=dict)


def _thematic(line: str) -> bool:
    match = re.fullmatch(r" {0,3}([*_\-])(?:[ \t]*\1){2,}[ \t]*", line)
    return bool(match)


def _atx(line: str):
    match = re.match(r"^ {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*)|[ \t]*$)", line)
    if not match:
        return None
    content = match.group(2) or ""
    if re.fullmatch(r"#+[ \t]*", content):
        content = ""
    content = re.sub(r"[ \t]+#+[ \t]*$", "", content).strip(" \t")
    return len(match.group(1)), content


def _quote_content(line: str) -> tuple[str, bool] | None:
    """Return quote content and whether the marked line is blank."""
    indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
    if indent > 3 or indent >= len(line) or line[indent] != ">":
        return None
    content = line[indent + 1:]
    # A single following space is part of the marker. A tab advances to the
    # next four-column stop; consume one column for the marker and retain the
    # remaining columns so indented code sees the original indentation.
    if content.startswith(" "):
        content = content[1:]
    elif content.startswith("\t"):
        # The tab begins one column after the marker, so it occupies three
        # columns in the source. The marker consumes one; remaining tabs keep
        # their original four-column stops, represented as spaces here.
        rest = content[1:]
        if rest.startswith("\t"):
            rest = "    " + rest[1:]
        content = "  " + rest.expandtabs(4)
    return content, not content.strip(" \t")


_LIST_MARKER = re.compile(r"^( {0,3})([-+*]|([0-9]{1,9})([.)]))([ \t]+|$)(.*)$")


def _list_marker(line: str):
    match = _LIST_MARKER.match(line)
    if not match:
        return None
    indent, marker, digits, delimiter, whitespace, rest = match.groups()
    if marker in "-*+" and _thematic(line):
        return None
    if marker in "*+" and re.fullmatch(r" {0,3}[ *_-](?:[ \t]*[ *_-]){2,}[ \t]*", line):
        return None

    start = int(digits) if ordered else 1
    if ordered and start > 999999999:
        return None
    width = len(indent) + len(marker)
    # The marker starts after ``indent`` columns. Tab stops are measured from
    # the beginning of the original line, so expanding the whitespace alone
    # from column zero overcounts tabs after a list marker.
    marker_column = len(indent) + len(marker)
    pad = 0
    for char in whitespace:
        pad += 4 - (marker_column + pad) % 4 if char == "\t" else 1
    if rest and pad > 4:
        rest = " " * (pad - 1) + rest
        pad = 1
    else:
        pad = max(1, pad)
    return (len(indent), marker if not ordered else delimiter, ordered, start, width + pad, rest, bool(rest.strip(" \t")))

import html.entities
import re

class Inline:

    literal: str = ""

_C1 = {

    0x85: 0x2026, 0x86: 0x2020, 0x87: 0x2021, 0x88: 0x02C6,
    0x89: 0x2030, 0x8A: 0x0160, 0x8B: 0x2039, 0x8C: 0x0152,
    0x8E: 0x017D, 0x91: 0x2018, 0x92: 0x2019, 0x93: 0x201C,
    0x94: 0x201D, 0x95: 0x2022, 0x96: 0x2013, 0x97: 0x2014,
    0x98: 0x02DC, 0x99: 0x2122, 0x9A: 0x0161, 0x9B: 0x203A,
    0x9C: 0x0153, 0x9E: 0x017E, 0x9F: 0x0178,

def _reference(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:

    if token.startswith("&#"):
        body = token[2:-1]
        try:
            value = int(body[1:], 16) if body[:1] in "xX" else int(body, 10)
        except ValueError:
            return token
        if value == 0 or value > 0x10FFFF or 0xD800 <= value <= 0xDFFF:
            value = 0xFFFD
        else:
            value = _C1.get(value, value)
        return chr(value)
    return html.entities.html5.get(token[1:], token)


def parse_inlines(source: str, references: dict) -> list[Inline]:

    del references  # Reserved for reference-link parsing in the inline pipeline.
    nodes: list[Inline] = []
    text: list[str] = []

    def flush() -> None:
        if text:
            value = "".join(text)
            if value:
                nodes.append(Inline("text", value))
            text.clear()

    i = 0
    while i < len(source):
        char = source[i]
        if char == "`":
            run_end = i + 1
            while run_end < len(source) and source[run_end] == "`":
                run_end += 1
            run_length = run_end - i
            search = run_end
            close_start = close_end = -1
            while search < len(source):
                candidate = source.find("`", search)
                if candidate < 0:
                    break
                candidate_end = candidate + 1
                while candidate_end < len(source) and source[candidate_end] == "`":
                    candidate_end += 1
                if candidate_end - candidate == run_length:
                    close_start, close_end = candidate, candidate_end
                    break
                search = candidate_end
            if close_start >= 0:
                flush()
                literal = source[run_end:close_start].replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").replace("\n", " ")
                if len(literal) >= 2 and literal.startswith(" ") and literal.endswith(" ") and literal.strip(" "):
                    literal = literal[1:-1]
                nodes.append(Inline("code", literal))
                i = close_end
            else:
                text.append(source[i:run_end])
                i = run_end
        elif char == "\\" and i + 1 < len(source) and source[i + 1] in _ASCII_PUNCTUATION:
            flush()
            # Keep escaped punctuation opaque to later delimiter processing.
            nodes.append(Inline("escaped", source[i + 1]))
            i += 2
        elif char == "&":
            match = _ENTITY.match(source, i)
            if match:
                text.append(_reference(match))
                i = match.end()
            else:
                text.append(char)
                i += 1
        elif char == "\n":

            nodes.append(Inline("softbreak"))
            i += 1
        else:

            i += 1

    # softbreak nodes unless resolving the joined source proves the break is
    # inside emphasis, in which case the newline belongs to that inline node.

    return _parse_emphasis(nodes)


def _contains_emphasis_newline(node: Inline) -> bool:
    return node.type in {"em", "strong"} and (
        "\n" in node.literal or any(_contains_emphasis_newline(child) for child in node.children or [])
        or any(child.type == "text" and "\n" in child.literal for child in node.children or [])

def _parse_emphasis(nodes: list[Inline]) -> list[Inline]:
    """Resolve delimiter runs in text nodes, leaving code spans opaque."""
    result: list[Inline] = []
    for node in nodes:
        if node.type != "text":
            result.append(node)
            continue
        source = node.literal
        # Match valid flanking pairs from the inside out. The pass only handles
        # delimiter characters; punctuation and Unicode whitespace use the
        # same flanking predicates as the CommonMark delimiter rules.
        chunks: list[Inline] = []
        i = 0
        plain = 0
        while i < len(source):
            if source[i] not in "*_":
                i += 1
                continue
            end = i + 1
            while end < len(source) and source[end] == source[i]:
                end += 1
            marker, length = source[i], end - i
            before = source[i - 1] if i else "\n"
            after = source[end] if end < len(source) else "\n"
            opener = not after.isspace() and (not _punct(after) or before.isspace() or _punct(before))
            closer = not before.isspace() and (not _punct(before) or after.isspace() or _punct(after))
            if marker == "_":
                opener = opener and (not closer or _punct(before))
                closer = closer and (not opener or _punct(after))
            if not opener:
                i = end
                continue
            close = end
            found = None
            while close < len(source):
                candidate = source.find(marker, close)
                if candidate < 0:
                    break
                ce = candidate + 1
                while ce < len(source) and source[ce] == marker:
                    ce += 1
                cb = source[candidate - 1] if candidate else "\n"
                ca = source[ce] if ce < len(source) else "\n"
                can_close = not cb.isspace() and (not _punct(cb) or ca.isspace() or _punct(ca))
                if marker == "_":
                    # Intraword underscores cannot close emphasis (the opener
                    # check already applies the corresponding left-flanking rule).
                    can_close = can_close and not (cb.isalnum() and ca.isalnum())
                use = 2 if length >= 2 and ce - candidate >= 2 else 1
                if can_close and candidate > end and not (marker == "_" and before.isalnum() and ca.isalnum()):
                    found = (candidate, ce, use)
                    break
                close = ce
            if found is None:
                i = end
                continue
            a, b, use = found
            prefix = source[plain:i] + marker * (length - use)
            if prefix:
                chunks.append(Inline("text", prefix))
            inner = _parse_emphasis([Inline("text", source[end:a])])
            chunks.append(Inline("strong" if use == 2 else "em", children=inner))
            source = source[:i] + source[end:a] + source[b:]
            i = i + (a - end)
            plain = i
        tail = source[plain:]
        if tail:
            chunks.append(Inline("text", tail))
        result.extend(chunks or [node])
    return result


def _punct(char: str) -> bool:
    return bool(char) and (char in _ASCII_PUNCTUATION or __import__("unicodedata").category(char).startswith("P"))

import html
import re

_LABEL = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}\[([^\[\]]+)\]:[ \t]*(.*)$")


def _unescape(value: str) -> str:
    value = html.unescape(value)
    return re.sub(r"\\([!\"#$%&'()*+,\-./:;<=>?@\[\\\]^_`{|}~])", r"\1", value)


def _label(value: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(value.casefold().strip(" \t\r\n").split())


def extract_definitions(text: str, references: dict) -> str:

    offset = 0

        match = _LABEL.match(current)
        if not match or not match.group(1).strip(" \t"):
            break

        first_definition = key not in references
        rest = match.group(2).strip(" \t")
        # Destinations and titles may continue on following lines. Keep the
        # original indentation available while applying the CommonMark limits.
        if not rest and offset + 1 < len(lines):
            candidate = lines[offset + 1].strip(" \t\r\n")

                rest = candidate
                offset += 1
        if rest and rest[0] in "\"'(" and rest[-1] != ({'"': '"', "'": "'", "(": ")"}[rest[0]]) and offset + 1 < len(lines):
            candidate = lines[offset + 1].strip(" \t\r\n")
            if candidate:
                rest += " " + candidate
                offset += 1
        destination = None
        title = None
        if rest.startswith("<"):
            end = rest.find(">")
            if end > 0 and "\n" not in rest[1:end]:
                destination, tail = rest[1:end], rest[end + 1:].strip(" \t")
            else:
                break
        else:
            dest_match = re.match(r"((?:\\.|[^\s])*)", rest)
            destination = dest_match.group(1) if dest_match else ""
            tail = rest[len(destination):].strip(" \t")
            if destination.count("(") - destination.count(")") > 0:
                break
        if not destination:
            break
        if tail:
            if tail[0] not in "\"'(" or tail[-1] != ({'"': '"', "'": "'", "(": ")"}[tail[0]]):
                break
            title = _unescape(tail[1:-1])
        if first_definition:
            references[key] = (_unescape(destination), title)
        offset += 1
        if offset < len(lines) and lines[offset].lstrip(" \t").startswith(("\"", "'", "(")) and title is None:
            candidate = lines[offset].strip(" \t\r\n")
            if len(candidate) >= 2 and candidate[0] in "\"'(" and candidate[-1] == {'"': '"', "'": "'", "(": ")"}[candidate[0]]:
                if first_definition:
                    references[key] = (_unescape(destination), _unescape(candidate[1:-1]))
                offset += 1
    return "".join(lines[offset:])
